_about: Robert Seymour Conway (1864-1933), Hulme Professor of Latin at Manchester, raw IA OCR of Harvard Lectures on the Vergilian Age (Cambridge: Harvard University Press; London: Humphrey Milford, 1928; US public domain by date). His other books are not yet audited. Latin literary history (lane B, round dy: fifth IA subject sweep). No uids minted. Round dz (2026-10-23), raw IA: Verner's Law in Italy (1887), The Italic Dialects (Cambridge, 1897, 2 vols), his Pitt Press Livy II (1902), The Youth of Vergil (1915), New Studies of a Great Inheritance (1921) and The Making of Latin (1923). Not taken: Scenes from the Rudens of Plautus (1906), translated by members of the Manchester Classical Society, which he only arranged; his Oxford Livy text (Latin only); the Brugmann Comparative Grammar he co-translated (Indo-European linguistics); the Melandra Castle excavation report (many contributors).
